## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing: `app/cli.py:6` removes `--wait` outright, but the ADR added in this PR says `--wait` stays as an alias for one release and logs a deprecation warning. As a result, any existing invocation that uses `--wait` now exits with code 2. This review read the full diff, `app/cli.py`, `tests/test_cli.py` and the new ADR, and searched the repository for other uses of `wait`; nothing outside the ADR uses it. The JSON/CSV `--format` choices and the 30-second default are unchanged, as the PR body and ADR state.

## Changes
The PR renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout`, so the parsed attribute changes from `args.wait` to `args.timeout`. It updates the tests to match and adds ADR `docs/adr/007-timeout.md` describing the transition. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Keep `--wait` as a deprecated alias for `--timeout` — Running `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now fails with argparse's "unrecognized arguments" error and `SystemExit(2)`, because the old `add_argument("--wait", ...)` was replaced rather than aliased. This contradicts the ADR added in the same diff at `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." No test checks that `--wait` is still accepted or that it emits a warning; the updated tests only use `--timeout`. — Any existing script or user passing `--wait` breaks immediately with no deprecation period and no message pointing to `--timeout`, even though the documented decision promises one release of compatibility. — Fix: Accept `--wait` as an alias with `dest="timeout"`, for example as a separate hidden argument or a custom action, and emit a `DeprecationWarning` or a stderr notice when it is used. Then add tests that `parse_args(["--wait", "12"]).timeout == 12` and that the warning fires.
